<c>D</c>icébat Ioánnes ad turbas, quæ éxibant ut baptizaréntur ab eo: Genímina viperárum, quis osténdit vobis fúgere a ventúra ira? <c>I</c>n the fifteenth year of the reign of Tiberius Caesar, Pontius Pilate being governor of Judea. And so on.

Homily by Pope St. Gregory (the Great)
<r>20th on the Gospels</r>
<c>J</c>ohn said unto the multitude, that came forth to be baptised of him: O generation of vipers, who hath warned you to flee from the wrath to come? The wrath to come in one sense signifieth the great vengeance of the Latter Day the sinner that repenteth not of his sin now, will have no mean whereby to flee from punishment then. Let us remark that addressing evil children copying the example of evil parents, the Baptist calleth them a generation of vipers in that they were envious at the righteous, and persecuted them; that they repaid evil for evil; that they hunted out ways of harming their neighbours, in all these things following the pattern of carnal parents, the prophet likeneth them to a venomous brood hatched from a venomous stock.

<h>V</h>igília sancti Thomæ Apóstoli.
<h>R</h>omæ natális sancti Zephyríni, Papæ et Mártyris. Ipsíus tamen festum recólitur séptimo Kaléndas Septémbris.
<h>I</h>bídem pássio sancti Ignátii, Epíscopi et Mártyris; qui, tértius post beátum Petrum Apóstolum, Antiochénam rexit Ecclésiam. Hic, in persecutióne Traiáni, damnátus ad béstias, Romam vinctus míttitur; ibíque, circumsedénte Senátu, immaníssimis pœnárum supplíciis primo est afféctus, dehinc obiícitur leónibus, quorum déntibus præfocátus, hóstia Christi effícitur. Eius vero festívitas Kaléndis Februárii celebrátur.
<h>I</h>tem Romæ sanctórum Mártyrum Liberáti et Báiuli.
<h>I</h>n Arábia sanctórum Mártyrum Eugénii et Macárii Presbyterórum, qui a Iuliáno Apóstata, cum ipsíus impietátem arguíssent, sævíssimis plagis affécti sunt, atque in vastíssimam erémum relegáti, et gládio cæsi.
<h>A</h>lexandríæ sanctórum mílitum et Mártyrum Ammónis, Zenónis, Ptolemǽi, Ingenis et Theóphili; qui, tribunálibus astántes, cum quidam Christiánus, in supplíciis pósitus, trepidáret et iam prope ad negándum declináret, vultu, óculis ac nútibus illum conabántur erígere. Cumque hac de causa clamor totíus pópuli in eos prosilíret, prorumpéntes in médium se Christiános esse testáti sunt; per quorum victóriam Christus, qui suis eam animi constántiam déderat, gloriosíssime triumphávit.
<h>G</h>éldubæ, in Germánia, sancti Iúlii Mártyris.
<h>A</h>ntiochíæ natális sancti Philogónii Epíscopi, qui, Dei nutu ex causídico ad eam Ecclésiam regéndam accersítus, advérsus Aríum, una cum sancto Alexándro Epíscopo et Sóciis, primum pro fide cathólica certámen íniit, clarúsque méritis quiévit in Dómino; cuius ánnuam festivitátem sanctus Ioánnes Chrysóstomus præcláro encómio celebrávit.
<h>B</h>ríxiæ sancti Domínici, Epíscopi et Confessóris.

b.d2a2cac49d:
<h>Martyrology</h>
<c>D</c>ecember 20th 2027, the 22nd day of the Moon,
<h>T</h>omorrow is the eve of the holy Apostle Thomas.
<h>U</h>pon the same 20th day of December, were born into the better life:
<h>A</h>t Rome, [in the year 219,] the holy Pope and martyr Zephyrinus, whose feast, however, is kept upon the 26th day of August.
<h>L</h>ikewise at Rome, the passion of the holy Bishop and martyr Ignatius, who ruled the church of Antioch as the third Bishop of that See in succession to the blessed Apostle Peter. In the persecution under the Emperor Trajan he was condemned to be killed by wild beasts, and was sent to Rome in chains. There, in the presence of the Senate, he was first put to most grievous torments and then thrown to lions, the which throttled him with their teeth, and so he was made Christ's offering, (in the year 107.) His feast, however, is kept upon the 1st day of February.
<h>A</h>t Rome, the holy martyrs Liberatus and Bajulus.
<h>I</h>n Arabia, the holy martyrs Eugenius and Macarius, two Priests who blamed the ungodliness of the Emperor Julian the Apostate, and for that cause were most cruelly flogged and sent out into the great desert, where they were slain with the sword, (in the year 362.)
<h>A</h>t Alexandria, the holy soldiers and martyrs Ammon, Zeno, Ptolemy, Ingenes, and Theophilus. They were on guard beside the judgment-seat when a certain Christian who was under the torture began to waver and was almost giving way, and they tried by signs to encourage him to hold out; for this cause all the people cried out against them, and they came forward and confessed themselves to be Christians and Christ, who Himself had given such steadfastness unto His own, did Himself most gloriously triumph in their victory, (in the year 249.)
<h>A</h>t Geldube, (in Thrace,) the holy martyr Julius, (fourth century.)
<h>A</h>t Antioch, holy Philogonius, Patriarch of the see. He was an advocate when he was called by the will of God to govern that church, and first took up the contending for the Catholic faith along with holy Bishop Alexander, and his Companions, against Arius. He fell asleep in the Lord, illustrious for good works, (in the year 322.) Holy John Chrysostom preached an eloquent sermon on his feast-day.
<h>A</h>t Brescia, the holy Confessor Dominic, Bishop (of that see, about the year 612.)
<h>O</h>n this day is commemorated the burial in Spain of holy Dominic, Abbot of Silos, (in the diocese of Burgos, in Castile, which abbey he founded,) of the Order of St. Benedict, very famous for his miracles wrought for the liberation of captives. (He died in his monastery at Silos, on December 14, 1073.)
<r>℣.</r> And elsewhere many other holy martyrs, confessors, and holy virgins.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.

<r>Ant.</r> O Root of Jesse, which standest for an ensign of the people, at whom the kings shall shut their mouths, to whom the Gentiles shall seek; come to deliver us, make no tarrying!
